nodes.title: Release 13 live (fa6f5a9, taxila-web--sfa6f5a9-glpk): the server recorder wrote NO lesson-flow rows. The API probe found 0 server events for its lesson at +6, +30 and +60 s (12.1: 13 kinds), the tier-2 browser proof found client events, blobs and request rows but no director.turn or model.call, and no '[trace] write failed' line appeared in Log Analytics. Lone authed and unauthenticated GETs were written. The same tree on the Neon TEST branch with the HTTP driver records everything, tier 2 included; production runs DB_DRIVER=pg, which this container cannot reach to reproduce

A buffered writer that drops a whole failed chunk and logs only its first 3 failures per process: one refused row hides every other row of its chunk, and the failure goes unseen once the first three are spent

Release 13.1: on a DATA error (SQLSTATE class 22/23) the trace writer halves the chunk until only the refused rows are left, which are dropped, counted (badRows) and named. A connection or timeout error still drops the chunk. Strings jsonb refuses (NUL, a lone surrogate from a cut mid-emoji) are replaced before buffering. Every failure is logged at most once a minute, and /api/health?trace=1 returns the counters (counts only). Reverse if: the counters show the loss is not a data error, and a different mechanism is found

md.measurements:
- `ms-r13-server-rows-lost-live` (2026-10-11, 21:13-21:40 UTC).
  - Release 13 (fa6f5a9) went live as taxila-web--sfa6f5a9-glpk (canary 4/4). Worker taxila-worker--wfa6f5a9-qbq4 with both jobs.
  - Tier-2 live proof (scratchpad r12-liveproof.mjs on taxila.dev):
    - recorded and stored: /api/me tier 2, the REC chip, 3 typed turns, a flag plus its note (flag.note), 8 rrweb chunks and 4 TTS clips in the private container, and the replay PNG;
    - the page's server request rows up to GET /api/child/map;
    - after the account delete: 0 rows.
    - Missing: every server row of the lesson itself (lesson start, turns, director.turn, model.call).
  - API probe (scratchpad srvtrace-probe2.mjs: a fresh @taxila.test account, lesson start plus one turn, counts at +6, +30 and +60 s before cleanup): 0 rows for the account each time. The same probe on 12.1 at 19:27 found 13 kinds (ms-r121-live).
  - Still written:
    - unauthenticated GET /api/me (3 requests, 21:35:06);
    - authed GET /api/me on a fresh account: 3 srv.req and 3 srv.res with its gid (scratchpad authrow.mjs).
  - The last server rows before those were the canary's and the proof's signups at 21:13:49 and 21:14:36.
  - No '[trace] write failed', 'dropped', 'failed', 'pool' or 'error' line from revision sfa6f5a9 in ContainerAppConsoleLogs_CL for the hour. The writer logs only failures 1-3 and every 50th.
  - Ruled out:
    - env var names: identical, 44 on 12.1 and on 13;
    - the existence filter: it keeps a real guardian and child (read-only check);
    - the recorder hooks in turn.js: intact;
    - writer.js and db.js: unchanged since 12.1.
  - Not reproduced here: the same tree on the Neon TEST branch, served by the packaged production server with the proof account at tier 2, recorded everything: 3 turns gave director.turn x3, classify, safety and db.write x3, srv x25 and model.call x18 with prompt blobs. Production runs DB_DRIVER=pg, and pg over TCP cannot connect from this container (timeout), so the pg path could not be reproduced.
  - A revision restart (ARM revisions/restart) did not bring the lesson rows back.
  - Release 13.1 makes the most likely mechanism impossible (dc-r131-writer-split-and-scrub) and makes it visible either way, through the /api/health?trace=1 counters and a log line for every failure, at most one a minute. The cause is confirmed or ruled out after deploy.
md.rejected: - `rj-r13-silent-chunk-drop` (2026-10-11). Tried: release 12's trace writer inserted 400 rows per statement, dropped the whole chunk on any error, logged failures 1-3 and then every 50th, and exposed no counters. What broke: release 13 in production lost every lesson-flow server row with nothing in the logs (ms-r13-server-rows-lost-live). There was no way to tell from outside which row or error, if any, was to blame. Instead: split on data errors, scrub what jsonb refuses, log every failure at most once a minute with its kinds, and expose the counters.
md.decisions:
- `dc-r131-writer-split-and-scrub` (2026-10-11).
  - What: on a Postgres data or integrity error (SQLSTATE class 22 or 23, or the message), the trace writer halves the failed chunk until only refused rows are left. Those are dropped, counted (traceStats().badRows) and named in the log (kind plus error). A connection or timeout error drops the chunk as before, so a dead database never becomes hundreds of retries.
  - record() replaces NUL and lone UTF-16 surrogates (left by any cut mid-emoji) with U+FFFD before buffering.
  - Every failure is logged, at most once a minute after the first three, with the chunk's kinds.
  - /api/health?trace=1 returns { buffered, dropped, written, failures, badRows }: counts only, never an event or an error text, because an error can quote a value.
  - Why: a recorder that loses events silently is worse than none, because it reads as the truth.
  - Tests: tests/r131-trace-writer.test.mjs (split, no split on connection errors, scrub), r12-trace-unit (the old behaviour kept).
  - Reverse if: the live counters show the loss is not a data error. Then the mechanism is elsewhere and this release only made it visible.
